comparator.name: Arts and Culture Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official prospective-student pages establish one coherent 180-EC Arts and Culture Studies pathway for the forthcoming cohort: a fixed 60-EC first year; 30 EC of fixed second-year study plus two 15-EC Faculty of Arts minors; and a third year with 20 EC of fixed specialist and professional study, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuine free electives. The year pages identify their applicable years as 2027-2028, 2028-2029 and 2029-2030. The official factsheet identifies the English-taught target as an Arts and Culture Studies specialisation under CROHO 56823. The exact named route is therefore reconstructed, and no neutral route choice is required.

components.note: Genuine free-choice space that may include courses at Radboud or another university, an internship or study abroad.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces much of the art-history, film, literary-analysis and creative-communication study with political philosophy, comparative and international politics, empire, gender history, social movements, heritage and conflict. Twelve of the 24 courses differ, and culture is organised around identity and power rather than broad analysis across artistic media.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes broad art-history coverage, Renaissance study, sociology, social theory and historical research. It adds rhetoric, world archaeology, environmental media, philosophy and advanced persuasive communication, with five courses differing from the closest match and fourteen from the identity-and-power route. The organising emphasis is interpretation and communication across text and screen.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad cross-arts, visual-art, theory, historical, international and research interests. Two further generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible at UCR: culture, identity and power; and literature, film and cultural communication. The pairwise differences range from five to fourteen courses, and each route has a distinct academic organisation. A further curating, exhibitions and cultural-field-practice direction remains evidenced, but the maximum of three alternatives has been reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce close visual analysis and interpretation of artworks in historical context.
Both examine visual culture and the institutions that shape modern artistic meaning; UCR focuses specifically on modern art and museums.
Both analyse material objects as cultural evidence across historical and social contexts; UCR uses world archaeology as its disciplinary frame.
UCR has heritage and material-culture courses but no single scheduled course centred on spatial culture.
Both provide foundational analysis and interpretation of written cultural texts.
Both provide substantive analysis of screen culture, film form and the social and political contexts of moving images.
Both study how stories and meanings move between media; UCR focuses on adaptation between literature and film.

Both place cultural and social transformation in European and wider historical context, though UCR is a general modern-history course.

Both require sustained independent research, source analysis and a substantial written argument; UCR's seminar is course-based rather than a separate thesis.

notes.text: Both programmes study art and culture through history, theory, interpretation, media and research. The Radboud programme additionally requires dedicated analysis of music and music as technology, two Faculty of Arts minors, professional festival work and substantial free-choice space. UCR offers strong combinations in art history, literature, film and media, communication, history, philosophy, sociology and politics, but no dedicated music-analysis sequence.
